scientific_rationale: The parent pointwise operator builds its local Hungarian correspondence from a purely geometric cost (assignment_element_cost=0.0), so a matched generated atom can be paired to a teacher ligand point of a different element. The registered factor assignment_element_cost adds a detached element-likelihood term to that cost matrix; it changes which generated atom receives the pseudo-Huber pull, not the pull's curvature or the native dose. V01 sets this coefficient to 0.5, a single-factor change from the parent value 0.0 with all other registered factors (operator, controller, dose.native_rms_ratio, dose.pointcloud_delta_A, band_multiplier, representation, window, steps, teacher_time) held at parent values and chemical graphs left free. This is a conditional correspondence hypothesis: it does not assert that element identity is a hydrogen-bond role, that any element channel carries interaction energy, or that the cost term is a direct elemental force. The parent response supplies the measured baseline for the same program and region: 40 active and 40 nonzero updates, assignment_switch_fraction mean 0.00203 (max 0.01667, last 0.0), atom_clip_fraction and cumulative_clip_fraction 0.0 throughout, point_rms_A mean 0.16918 A falling from 0.40217 to 0.03942, injected_rms_A_mean 0.03011 A, current_gradient_rms_mean 0.00503.
